---
title: "Examples"
subtitle: "The configurations worth knowing."
description: "Spotlight configurations for a room, a stream, and a bright projector, with what each changes."
---

The [preview deck](preview.html) is built by this site with the first of these.
A spotlight is a thing that moves, so the deck is the only place any of this can be judged: open it and hold the mouse button down.

## A spotlight for a recording

```yaml
format:
  revealjs:
    spotlight:
      size: 90
      presentingCursor: "default"
revealjs-plugins:
  - spotlight
```

A larger radius reads better once a slide is scaled down into a video frame, and keeping an ordinary cursor visible means the audience can follow the pointer even when the spotlight is off.

## A coloured pointer for a bright room

```yaml
format:
  revealjs:
    spotlight:
      useAsPointer: true
      pointerColor: "#b22222"
      size: 30
```

Dimming works badly on a washed-out projector.
`useAsPointer` draws a coloured dot instead, which survives the room.

## Triggered by a key rather than the mouse

```yaml
format:
  revealjs:
    spotlight:
      toggleSpotlightOnMouseDown: false
      spotlightOnKeyPressAndHold: 73
```

Useful with a presenter remote that sends a key rather than a click.
The value is a legacy `keyCode`, so 73 is <kbd>I</kbd>; `false` disables the behaviour.
The deck still has to be in presentation mode for the key to reach the plugin.

## Keeping the pointer on the slide

```yaml
format:
  revealjs:
    spotlight:
      lockPointerInsideCanvas: true
```

Holds the pointer inside the presentation on a multi-monitor setup, through the Pointer Lock API.
A browser may refuse it without a user gesture first.

## Turning off the fade

```yaml
format:
  revealjs:
    spotlight:
      fadeInAndOut: 0
```

The spotlight then appears and disappears at once, which some find easier to follow than a fade.

## A crosshair while the spotlight is on

```yaml
format:
  revealjs:
    spotlight:
      spotlightCursor: "crosshair"
      presentingCursor: "default"
```

`spotlightCursor` applies only while the spotlight is on, and `presentingCursor` applies the rest of the time.
This pair shows an ordinary cursor while you talk, then a crosshair at the centre of the lit circle while you hold the mouse button down.
The value goes straight into the `cursor` style of the page, so any CSS cursor keyword works.
`lockPointerInsideCanvas` overrides both, because the Pointer Lock API hides the pointer itself.

## A deck whose text stays selectable

```yaml
format:
  revealjs:
    spotlight:
      disablingUserSelect: false
```

The plugin turns text selection off when the deck enters [presentation mode](reference.html#presentation-mode), and turns it back on when the deck leaves.
A deck that never leaves presentation mode therefore keeps its text unselectable from the first slide to the last, code blocks included.
Set `disablingUserSelect` to `false` and the plugin leaves selection alone.
Nothing else changes: presentation mode still sets the cursor from `presentingCursor`, and the mouse button still turns the spotlight on.

## A deck that starts as an ordinary page

```yaml
format:
  revealjs:
    include-after-body: presentation-mode.html
    spotlight:
      initialPresentationMode: false
```

`initialPresentationMode: false` starts the deck outside presentation mode.
The cursor stays visible, the text stays selectable, and neither the mouse button nor the held key turns the spotlight on.
The deck therefore reads as an ordinary web page until you ask for the spotlight.
`RevealSpotlight.togglePresentationMode()` is the only way in, so give the deck a control of its own.
Save this as `presentation-mode.html` beside the deck:

```html
<script>
  window.addEventListener("keydown", function (event) {
    if (event.altKey && event.code === "KeyP") {
      RevealSpotlight.togglePresentationMode();
    }
  });
</script>
```

<kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>P</kbd> then switches presentation mode on and off.
Pick a key the deck does not already use.
The listener reads `event.code`, which a modifier key does not change.

## A spotlight that stays on

```yaml
format:
  revealjs:
    include-after-body: latching-spotlight.html
    spotlight:
      toggleSpotlightOnMouseDown: false
      presentingCursor: "default"
```

A held mouse button suits a quick gesture, not a long explanation.
`RevealSpotlight.toggleSpotlight()` switches the spotlight and leaves it there.
Save this as `latching-spotlight.html` beside the deck:

```html
<script>
  window.addEventListener("keydown", function (event) {
    if (event.altKey && event.code === "KeyS") {
      RevealSpotlight.toggleSpotlight();
    }
  });
</script>
```

The plugin draws the spotlight at the last pointer position it saw, so move the pointer once after the deck loads.
This call does not test presentation mode, and it hands the cursor back to `presentingCursor` every time it switches the spotlight off.
Give `presentingCursor` a visible value, as above, if the deck can also be outside presentation mode.
